guide.title: Fordham Heights, the Bronx: The Concourse and the Paradise
guide.intro: Fordham Heights is the name Wikipedia's station infoboxes attach to the Grand Concourse between East 182nd Street and Fordham Road, and it sits in Bronx Community District 5, whose stated limits are Webster Avenue to the east and Fordham Road to the north. The boulevard it is strung along was conceived in 1890 by Louis Aloys Risse, an immigrant from Saint-Avold in Lorraine, and built between 1894 and 1909, 180 feet wide for most of its 5.2 miles. By the mid-1930s almost three hundred apartment buildings stood along it, in Art Deco and Art Moderne. Fordham Road crosses here in a grade-separated junction, carrying what its own article calls the borough's largest and most diverse shopping district. Loew's Paradise Theatre opened at 2403 Grand Concourse on September 7, 1929.

sections.heading: The Concourse, the shopping district and the Paradise
sections.body:
Louis Aloys Risse first conceived of the Grand Concourse in 1890, and it was built between 1894 and 1909, with a southward extension in 1927, at a total cost of $14 million. It runs 5.2 miles from East 138th Street to Mosholu Parkway, 180 feet wide for most of that distance, and passes through Bedford Park, Concourse, Highbridge, Fordham, Mott Haven, Norwood and Tremont. At Fordham Road the main road passes underneath in a grade-separated junction while the service roads meet the cross street at grade.

Fordham Road itself runs west-east for 2.4 miles from the Harlem River to Bronx Park, a two-way, four-lane road that divides into East and West Fordham Road at Jerome Avenue, with house numbers rising away from Jerome in both directions. Wikipedia describes it as geographically separating the North Bronx from the South Bronx and as housing the borough's largest and most diverse shopping district. That district is managed by the Fordham Road Business Improvement District, a non-profit organization under contract with the City of New York, which maintains, develops and markets the merchants along the road and hosts community events; the district it covers stretches from Third and Webster Avenues west to Jerome Avenue, and Fordham's own article puts the business improvement district on the northern border of the neighborhood and calls the retail district the longest in the Bronx.

John Eberson's Loew's Paradise Theatre opened on the Concourse on September 7, 1929, an atmospheric theatre with an Italian Baroque design and seating for about 3,885. Its exterior was designated a New York City Landmark on April 15, 1997, and its lobbies and auditorium interior on May 16, 2006.

Monroe University's campus has been in the Fordham neighborhood since 1967, seven buildings near the shopping district. The school began somewhere else entirely: Mildred King founded it in 1933 as the Monroe School of Business, a women's business school in the West Farms section of the Bronx, and it was 1977 before the West Farms facilities closed and all its programs were consolidated in the Fordham Road area.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body:
Two IND Concourse Line stations run under the Grand Concourse here, and Wikipedia gives the locale of both as Fordham Heights. Fordham Road, at East Fordham Road and the Grand Concourse, is served by the D at all times and the B on weekdays. 182nd–183rd Streets, at East 182nd Street and the Grand Concourse, is served by the D at all times except peak-direction rush hours and by the B on weekdays. Both opened on July 1, 1933 with the rest of the Concourse subway.

The IRT Jerome Avenue Line has a Fordham Road station of its own, at Fordham Road and Jerome Avenue, served by the 4 and opened on June 2, 1917; its article places it in the University Heights and Fordham neighborhoods. It has stairs to all four corners and an elevator at the southeast corner.

Metro-North's Fordham station is at 417 East Fordham Road, on the Harlem Line and the New Haven Line, and opened on March 1, 1841. It has two below-ground side platforms eight cars long, serving the outer tracks of a four-track main line, and is part of the Fordham Plaza complex — which Fordham Road's own article places east of Webster Avenue, and Webster Avenue is Community District 5's stated eastern limit.

The bus routes named for the IRT's Fordham Road station are the Bx12, Bx12 SBS and Bx32. Metro-North's Fordham station is served by the Bx9, Bx12, Bx12 SBS, Bx15, Bx17, Bx22, Bx41 and Bx41 SBS, and by Bee-Line routes 60, 61 and 62.

This page does not name a ferry landing for Fordham Heights.

faq.question: How do I get to Fordham Heights?
faq.answer: By subway most directly. The IND Concourse Line runs under the Grand Concourse, and Wikipedia gives the locale of two of its stations as Fordham Heights: Fordham Road, at East Fordham Road and the Grand Concourse, and 182nd–183rd Streets, at East 182nd Street. The D calls at both at all times, except that it skips 182nd–183rd Streets in the peak direction at rush hours; the B calls at both on weekdays. The IRT Jerome Avenue Line's separate Fordham Road station, at Jerome Avenue, is served by the 4 and is placed by its own article in the University Heights and Fordham neighborhoods. On Metro-North, Fordham station at 417 East Fordham Road is on the Harlem Line and the New Haven Line, in the Fordham Plaza complex east of Webster Avenue. The buses named for those two stations are the Bx9, Bx12, Bx12 SBS, Bx15, Bx17, Bx22, Bx32, Bx41 and Bx41 SBS, plus Bee-Line routes 60, 61 and 62. This page does not name a ferry landing for Fordham Heights.

faq.question: Can you see a film at the Paradise Theater?
faq.answer: This page makes no claim about what the building holds today. Loew's Paradise Theatre opened at 2403 Grand Concourse on September 7, 1929, an atmospheric theatre by John Eberson seating about 3,885, and 3,855 as of 2012. It was leased in October 2012 to World Changers Church International, which vacated it in 2020; it was vacant as of 2023, and the Bronx Independent Cinema Center began hosting events there in 2025. The exterior and the interior carry separate city landmark designations, from 1997 and 2006.

faq.question: What is the Fordham Road shopping district?
faq.answer: The retail strip along Fordham Road, which Wikipedia's article on the road calls the borough's largest and most diverse shopping district and Fordham's own article calls the longest in the Bronx. It is managed by the Fordham Road Business Improvement District, a non-profit organization under contract with the City of New York, whose district stretches from Third and Webster Avenues west to Jerome Avenue. Monroe University's article puts the shopping district at about 80 buildings housing nearly 300 businesses.

places.name: Grand Concourse
places.summary: The 5.2-mile boulevard running from East 138th Street to Mosholu Parkway, 180 feet wide for most of its length and passing through Bedford Park, Concourse, Highbridge, Fordham, Mott Haven, Norwood and Tremont. At Fordham Road the main road passes underneath in a grade-separated junction while the service roads intersect with the cross street.
places.history: Louis Aloys Risse, an immigrant from Saint-Avold in Lorraine, France, first conceived of the road in 1890; it was built between 1894 and 1909, with a southward extension in 1927, at a total cost of $14 million. By the mid-1930s almost three hundred apartment buildings had been constructed along it, in Art Deco and Art Moderne. In 1939 it was called "the Park Avenue of middle-class Bronx residents," a phrase the source attributes to that year's WPA guide.

places.name: Paradise Theater
places.summary: The movie palace at 2403 Grand Concourse, opened as Loew's Paradise Theatre on September 7, 1929 to a design by John Eberson: an atmospheric theatre with an Italian Baroque design. Original seating was about 3,885, and 3,855 as of 2012.
places.history: The exterior was designated a New York City Landmark on April 15, 1997, reference number 1891, and the lobbies and auditorium interior separately on May 16, 2006, reference number 2193. The building was leased in October 2012 to World Changers Church International, which vacated it in 2020; it was vacant as of 2023, and the Bronx Independent Cinema Center began hosting events there in 2025. Its own article places it close to the Fordham Road station of the IND Concourse Line.

places.name: Fordham Road Business Improvement District
places.summary: A non-profit organization under contract with the City of New York which maintains, develops and markets the merchants along Fordham Road and hosts community events. Its district stretches from Third and Webster Avenues west to Jerome Avenue, along the strip Wikipedia's article on the road calls the borough's largest and most diverse shopping district.
places.history: Fordham's own article calls the retail district the longest in the Bronx and records that the business improvement district operates on the northern border of the neighborhood. Monroe University's article gives the shopping district as about 80 buildings housing nearly 300 businesses. Fordham Road runs 2.4 miles west-east from the Harlem River to Bronx Park, dividing into East and West Fordham Road at Jerome Avenue.

places.name: Monroe University
places.summary: A private university whose campus has been in the Fordham neighborhood of the Bronx since 1967, in seven buildings near the Fordham shopping district. It also maintains campuses in New Rochelle, New York and in Saint Lucia.
places.history: Mildred King founded the school in 1933 as the Monroe School of Business, a women's business school in the West Farms section of the Bronx. In 1977 the West Farms facilities were closed and all Monroe programs were consolidated in the Fordham Road area.

links.note: Wikipedia gives Fordham Road as Belmont's northern boundary, and the Fordham Road shopping district runs along that line.
Fordham Road ends east at Bronx Park, whose northwestern edge is Webster Avenue — Community District 5's stated eastern limit.
Loew's Paradise opened in 1929, the year the Loew's Pitkin Theatre was built in Brownsville: two movie palaces on the same circuit.
